justification: A public-label change: the address page header and tagline now say Council Rules and drop an overclaim, with a test that the old name is not used on that page

falsifiable_check.fails_when: The address page source contains the retired name Site Controls
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Before the rename the new test failed on the address page; after it the test passes

pre_impl.existing_data: No data is read or written; this is a label and tagline in one page component
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: If the page file moves the test cannot find it and fails loudly rather than passing
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Applies to every address page view after deploy
pre_impl.frontend_type: No type changes; two text strings
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: A visitor now sees Council Rules as the page name, matching the homepage and the menu

functions.name: AssessmentPage
functions.input: no props, a client page component
functions.output: the address page with the Council Rules header
functions.if_none: there are no inputs, so nothing can be missing

values.if_missing: the header still renders and the body shows the empty state

break_it.scenario: A later edit restores the old header text
break_it.what_happens: The product names test fails and CI blocks the change
break_it.how: The test reads the page source for the retired name

break_it.scenario: The old name remains on unlisted for pages
break_it.what_happens: Those unlinked pages still say Site Controls
break_it.how: Known limit: the for pages are unlisted and noindex and were not edited

break_it.scenario: The tagline claims too much for a table with unchecked citations
break_it.what_happens: The new tagline makes no claim about every control being cited
break_it.how: The tagline now only says what the page is

post_merge.manual_verify: Open /assessment and read the header: it says Council Rules and the new tagline
